messages.author: 9ccdef93cb3041c6
messages.subject: faceted CI
parts:
Dear all,

I'm trying to plot the CI on a ggplot on several facets.
As an example:

ggplot(data=diamonds) +
geom_point(alpha=0.6) +
aes(x=price, y=carat, colour=cut) +
facet_wrap(~ color, ncol=1, scales="free")

Here, I have the data colored by cut and faceted by color.
What I'm looking for is to plot the CI (quantiles) on each facet
independently, but using all the data in each facet (that is, not
splited by cut).

I tried playing with stat_summary and fun.ymin and fun.ymax but no good..

any idea?
thanks
FGV

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: faceted CI
parts:
A simple way to do this is to compute the quantiles outside of ggplot2
and import them in the ggplot() call. The key is having a variable in
that data frame which matches the faceting variable.

library(plyr)
library(reshape2)
colorCI <- ddply(diamonds, "color", summarise,
ll = quantile(price, .025),
ul = quantile(price, 0.975))
colorCIm <- melt(colorCI, id = "color")
str(colorCIm)

ggplot(data=diamonds) +
geom_point(aes(x=price, y=carat, colour=cut), alpha=0.6) +
geom_vline(data = colorCIm, aes(xintercept = value), color = "blue") +
facet_wrap(~ color, ncol=1, scales="free_y")

Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: faceted CI
parts:
Hi again:

If your intention was to fit regression quantiles by cut for each
color instead, here's a simpl[e/istic] way to use stat_quantile() for
your example:

qs <- c(0.025, 0.975)
ggplot(data = diamonds, aes(x=price, y=carat, colour=cut)) +
geom_point(alpha=0.6) +
stat_quantile(quantiles = qs) +

I kept the same color scheme for the line colors. This is a busy plot,
though, so if this is what you were really after, you might consider
ways to simplify the display (e.g., reduce the point size and/or
increase the size of the lines).

Dennis
